title: CapabilityManifest
description:
SPEC 7.4. Every field here appears in that section's worked example; nothing is invented.

Two invariants the installer must uphold and this schema cannot express (SPEC 7.4, 13.1): installation is idempotent, so re-running is a no-op; and it is removable, so files and env go while data tables stay with a warning. A failed smoke_check rolls the whole install back as one unit.

Enums appear where SPEC enumerates the values. Where SPEC shows one member of an obviously open set — provision.kind, provision.completion — the field is a patterned string instead, because inventing the rest of the enum would violate SPEC 0 rule 5 and force a churn commit later.

id.description: Primary key in SPEC 6 capabilities. v1 catalogue (SPEC 13.2): auth, payments, email, uploads, slack, ai.

version.description: Semver. Installs resolve a pinned version (SPEC 13.1 step 1), never a range.

summary.description: One line for the catalogue. SPEC 6 capabilities.summary.

framework.description: Compatibility ranges checked against the project before install (SPEC 13.1 step 1). Keyed by framework name; SPEC 7.4 shows {"next": ">=15 <16"}.

credential_owner.title: CredentialOwner
credential_owner.description: SPEC 6 and 13.2. `builder` means the project owner connects their own account, so one credential lives in our secret store. `runtime` means each end user of the generated app connects their own, which needs a token table in the app's database, callback routes, per-app encryption and refresh handling. SPEC 13.2: ship builder-time only in v1.

kind.description: What backing resource to create. SPEC 7.4 shows `stripe_connect`; SPEC 13.2 implies app-database tables, a sending domain, an R2 bucket and workspace OAuth.

completion.description: How provisioning finishes when it cannot finish synchronously. SPEC 7.4 shows `hosted_onboarding`, which surfaces as project_capabilities.state = needs_action.

produces.description: Keys this step writes into project_capabilities.external_refs (SPEC 6).

dependencies.description: npm packages added to the project, name to semver range.

template.description: Template file within the capability module.

on_conflict.title: OnConflict
on_conflict.description: What to do when `path` already exists. SPEC 7.4 uses `skip` for route handlers the user may have edited and `overwrite` for generated library glue.

additive.description: SPEC 12.5: a migration that dropped a column cannot be undone by adding a commit, so capability migrations must be additive. `false` requires an approved proposals row before it runs.

scope.title: EnvScope
scope.description: SPEC 17.2: a `server` value must never reach the client bundle.

from.description: Where the value comes from, e.g. `provision.secret_key`.

dev_variant.description: SPEC 13.1 step 4 and 17.1: development scope gets this variant, so only a test-mode key ever reaches a sandbox. A prompt injection that exfiltrates a sandbox environment then burns a test key.

relay_path.description: SPEC 13.3: third-party webhooks cannot target a sandbox tunnel, whose URL changes on every create and every restore - Modal assigns a random hostname and offers no way to pin one - so they hit a stable relay that forwards to whichever preview is live and queues with replay when none is.

smoke_check.description: SPEC 13.1 step 5: run against the preview after install. Failure rolls the whole install back as one unit. Modelled as a union so a new kind is an additive change.

drop_tables.description: SPEC 7.4 and 13.1: data tables stay with a warning. `true` is a destructive migration and needs an approved proposal (SPEC 12.5).
